rules.qualification: The model uses only learned embeddings, attention, MLPs, a straight-through categorical state, and evaluator-owned endpoint cross-entropy. It has no programmed arithmetic, product table, carry, quotient, remainder, integer reconstruction, synthetic data, cross-batch cache, or participant-owned training loop.

hypothesis: Exact identity initialization, dynamic microdepth, immutable input recall, strict macrostep boundaries, straight-through discrete state, and scratch reset can make a small tied processor learn a reusable transition instead of a fixed computation depth.

validation.cpu_smoke: training and one test evaluation completed; the manifest's 0.05-second CPU evaluation budget then expired

correction_history: Before submission, one test syntax bracket was corrected, a naive forbidden-word check was narrowed to prohibited executable mechanisms, and the expected local state count was corrected to the measured 234624. The candidate architecture and training contract did not change.
conclusion: The low and similar train, test, and OOD cross-entropy shows stable marginal prediction, but exact T1 transfer was zero on both profiles. The fixed mechanism did not learn a reusable transition.
limitation: One Easy E5 seed and 901 updates. This rejects the exact combined mechanism and contract, not all identity initialization or dynamic-depth recurrence.
no_retry_history: Do not submit an adjacent width, head, scratch-token, microdepth-range, learning-rate, batch, or seed variant without a new learning-mechanism hypothesis and new user authorization.
